claim: A CHECKER DEFECT WAS CAUGHT THAT REPORTED A CONTENT OMISSION WHERE NONE EXISTED, AND THE TWO ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE VERDICT LINE ALONE. verify_notice.py's main() read the notice in BINARY and decoded it, then matched fenced blocks with the pattern '```\n(.*?)```'. The file on disk has CRLF line endings, so the pattern matched nothing and the PSLQ check reported 'no fenced block containing the basis was found' -- verbally identical to what it would report if the basis had actually been omitted from the notice, which is precisely the failure the TRANSIT MANIFEST exists to prevent. It was caught only because a second, independent read of the same function in TEXT mode returned the block and passed, i.e. two reads of one file disagreed. Repair: normalise CRLF to LF immediately after decoding, in ONE place. GENERAL FORM: a check that reports ABSENCE cannot distinguish 'the content is missing' from 'my reader could not see it', so an absence report must be confirmed by a second reader before it is believed -- and the mutant controls do not catch this, because a broken reader rejects the mutant too, for the same wrong reason.
